hunks.baseline: Vague explanations from beginning to end, as if they were shrouded in fog.
hunks.sol: The whole description was vague, as if someone had hidden it in fog.

hunks.baseline: Of course, this wasn’t the first time I’d received a Quest like this. That didn’t make it any less impossible to get used to.
hunks.sol: This wasn’t the first time I’d received a Quest like this, of course. That didn’t make it any easier to get used to.

hunks.baseline: *This is a process I have to go through.*
hunks.sol: *It’s something I have to go through.*

hunks.baseline: It was more like a signpost, pointing me in a direction and telling me what lay beyond.
hunks.sol: It was more like a signpost, pointing me in a direction and telling me what lay ahead.

hunks.baseline: Depending on my choices, the arrows on the sign might change. Sometimes, like now, I had to interpret them myself.
hunks.sol: Depending on my choices, the arrows on that sign might change. Sometimes, like now, I had to figure out what they meant.

hunks.baseline: So I read the words in the holographic window again and again.
hunks.sol: So I read the words in the holographic window again and again, trying to work out what those Twenty Questions-style clues were hiding.

hunks.baseline: Trying to figure out the meaning hidden in those twenty-questions-style clues.

hunks.baseline: And in that regard, the last two sentences in the Quest description were more than enough to catch my eye.
hunks.sol: The last two sentences of the Quest description, in particular, caught my eye.

hunks.baseline: A year could feel like an eternity to a little kid with a runny nose, but to a white-haired old man, it might be no more than a fleeting moment.
hunks.sol: A year could feel long and distant to a little kid with a runny nose, but to a white-haired old man, it might pass in the blink of an eye.

hunks.baseline: So I had no way of guessing how much time the System meant by “not too distant.”
hunks.sol: I couldn’t guess how much time the System meant by “not too distant.”

hunks.baseline: A few days. A few months. Or… No. Even the System couldn’t be so shameless as to call it “not too distant” if it meant years.
hunks.sol: A few days. A few months. Or… No. Even the System couldn’t be so shameless as to lump years together under that phrase.

hunks.baseline: *Days would be too soon, and years would be too long. It makes sense to take it as something that’ll happen within a few months.*
hunks.sol: *Days would be too soon, and years would be too long. A few months seems like the reasonable guess.*

hunks.baseline: Then what was that last line about it not being an unhappy moment?
hunks.sol: Then what was that last line about the meeting not being unhappy?

hunks.baseline: And who on earth was the owner of that unknown voice—the very person who’d brought about this riddle of a Quest?
hunks.sol: And who on earth was the owner of that unknown voice—the person at the heart of this riddle of a Quest?

hunks.baseline: *Someone who could approach me without being noticed by me, the Thunderbolt Saber King, or even the Old Master. Someone who could intrude into my private inner world.*
hunks.sol: *Someone who could approach without me, the Thunderbolt Saber King, or even the Old Master noticing. Someone who could intrude into my own inner world.*

hunks.baseline: When Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body was taking place, the Thunderbolt Saber King and I were too busy giving and receiving energy to do much else. But Jeok Cheongang was different.
hunks.sol: While Transmitting Internal Energy Across the Body was underway, the Thunderbolt Saber King and I had our hands full giving and receiving energy. But Jeok Cheongang was different.

hunks.baseline: He’d stood guard for this dangerous technique, and he’d been straining every sense he had.
hunks.sol: He’d stood guard throughout that dangerous technique, every sense strained to its limit.

hunks.baseline: It should’ve been impossible to evade his notice and speak to me—especially when he was a Supreme Peak master who now stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints, beyond even the Ten Kings.
hunks.sol: For someone to evade his notice and speak to me should have been impossible. He was a Supreme Peak master who now stood shoulder to shoulder with the Three Saints, beyond even the Ten Kings.

hunks.baseline: Well, strictly speaking, it wasn’t completely impossible.
hunks.sol: Well, strictly speaking, it wasn’t *completely* impossible.

hunks.baseline: *If they were the greatest assassin of all time, with a concealment technique without precedent, or a master at least two moves ahead of the Old Master…*
hunks.sol: *If they were the greatest assassin of all time, with a concealment technique unlike anything ever seen before—or a master at least two moves ahead of the Old Master…*

hunks.baseline: And as far as I knew, only two people in the world could meet even those minimum requirements.
hunks.sol: As far as I knew, only two people in the world could meet those minimum requirements.

hunks.baseline: The first was undoubtedly the greatest assassin of all time, but I couldn’t think of a reason they’d do something like this—or be sure they could pull it off.
hunks.sol: The first was undoubtedly the greatest assassin of all time, but I couldn’t be sure they had any reason to do this—or that they could pull it off.

hunks.baseline: But the other one was different.
hunks.sol: The other one was different.

hunks.baseline: A wonder of the entire world.
hunks.sol: A wonder of the world itself.

hunks.baseline: The sky itself, looking down over this vast land alone. A being who, though born human, had come to be called a god.
hunks.sol: The sky looking down over this vast land alone. A being who, though human, had come to be called a god.

hunks.baseline: “……The Martial God?”
hunks.sol: “…The Martial God?”

hunks.baseline: The two syllables slipped from my lips before I realized it. A shiver ran down my spine.
hunks.sol: The name slipped from my lips before I realized it. A shiver ran down my spine.

hunks.baseline: He’d vanished as suddenly as he’d appeared in the world, and no one under heaven knew where he was now.
hunks.sol: He’d vanished as suddenly as he’d first appeared, and no one under heaven knew where he was now.

hunks.baseline: Not even the Bow Saint, who’d found me through the letter the Martial God had left behind.
hunks.sol: Not even the Bow Saint, who’d found me through the letter he’d left behind.

hunks.baseline: But realistically, the only person who could’ve done something like this was the Martial God.
hunks.sol: But realistically, the Martial God was the only person capable of what had happened today.

hunks.baseline: As far as I knew, he alone was an overwhelming presence beyond the superhumans known as the Three Saints.
hunks.sol: As far as I knew, he alone was an overwhelming presence beyond even the superhumans known as the Three Saints.

hunks.baseline: And perhaps I was the only person under heaven who knew more than anyone else about the truth hidden behind the Martial God.
hunks.sol: And perhaps I knew more about the truth hidden behind the Martial God than anyone else under heaven.

hunks.baseline: The first deep conversation I’d had with the Bow Saint at the Imperial Palace.
hunks.sol: I remembered the first deep conversation I’d had with the Bow Saint at the Imperial Palace. Amid the hectic days that followed, there had been one name I could only turn over in the back of my mind.

hunks.baseline: Amid the hectic days that followed, the name of someone I could only turn over in the back of my mind filled my thoughts.
hunks.sol: Now it filled my thoughts.

hunks.baseline: Another absolute being who existed beyond a distant space.
hunks.sol: Another absolute being, existing beyond a distant space.

hunks.baseline: Just as the Martial God had opposed the Heavenly Demon and restored peace, he was a hero who’d saved humanity from the demon known as the Demon King Asmodeus.
hunks.sol: Just as the Martial God had fought the Heavenly Demon and restored peace, Cheon Taemin was a hero who’d saved humanity from the demon known as the Demon King Asmodeus.

hunks.baseline: I could still see him clearly: unconscious, seemingly deep asleep, hooked up to a life-support system combining Magic and science in the Ares Guild’s restricted area.
hunks.sol: I could still see him clearly in the Ares Guild’s restricted area, unconscious as if in a deep sleep, attached to a life-support system that combined Magic and science.

hunks.baseline: And over that image, the voice of a woman faintly overlapped.
hunks.sol: Over that image, I could faintly hear a woman’s voice.

hunks.baseline: That day, the Bow Saint’s eyes had been fixed on me, deep and solemn.
hunks.sol: That day, the Bow Saint had watched me with a deep, solemn gaze.

hunks.baseline: And then, that voice had echoed faintly in my ears like a distant refrain.
hunks.sol: Then her voice had echoed faintly in my ears, like a distant refrain.

hunks.baseline: No—I’d never forget it, even on my deathbed.
hunks.sol: No—I’d remember it until the day I died.

hunks.baseline: A piece of a puzzle I’d never imagined suddenly falling into place, after I’d turned it over vaguely in my mind and then laughed it off.
hunks.sol: I’d vaguely entertained the thought before, only to laugh at myself and shake my head. Then an unexpected piece of the puzzle had fallen into place.

hunks.baseline: The supernatural ability that belonged to me now—and to the Martial God in the past.
hunks.sol: The supernatural ability that belonged to me now—and had belonged to the Martial God in the past.

hunks.baseline: If the message the Martial God had left the Bow Saint was what I thought it was, that could mean only one thing.
hunks.sol: If the message the Martial God had left the Bow Saint meant what I thought it did, it could mean only one thing.

hunks.baseline: The truth hidden behind an unparalleled hero the likes of whom had never been seen before, and would never be seen again: a man who’d appeared out of nowhere, saved a world in turmoil, then disappeared.
hunks.sol: The truth hidden behind an unparalleled hero who’d appeared out of nowhere, saved a world in turmoil, then disappeared.

hunks.baseline: The moment I reached that thought, a headache came over me.
hunks.sol: The moment my thoughts reached that point, a headache struck.

hunks.baseline: Two heroes from separate worlds.
hunks.sol: Two heroes in different worlds.

hunks.baseline: Their actions were astonishingly alike, and the more I learned about them, the more I found myself wondering whether Cheon Taemin or the Martial God might have had the same ability as me.
hunks.sol: Their actions were astonishingly alike. The more I learned about them, the more I found myself wondering whether Cheon Taemin or the Martial God might have had the same ability as me. Whether the two of them might even be the same person.

hunks.baseline: Whether the two of them might be the same person.
But now I didn’t know anymore.
hunks.sol: But now I didn’t know what to think.

hunks.baseline: What connection, if any, existed between the Martial God and Cheon Taemin.

hunks.sol: Decision made, I lay straight on the bed and pulled the covers up to my neck.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know whose presence was hurrying toward me from somewhere in the distance beyond the window, but by the time they reached my room, all they’d find would be me already gone to the modern world—or, well, fast asleep.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know whose presence was hurrying toward me from somewhere far beyond the window, but by the time they reached my room, all they’d find was me already gone to the modern world—or rather, fast asleep.

hunks.baseline: I slowly closed my eyes and recited the familiar command. The next moment, I realized something.
hunks.sol: I slowly closed my eyes and gave the familiar command. The next moment, I realized something.

hunks.baseline: ……What?
hunks.sol: …What?

hunks.baseline: My eyes flew open, even though I hadn’t meant to open them.
hunks.sol: My eyes flew open.

hunks.baseline: But neither the System’s voice that had pierced my ears nor the dozens of error messages floating in the air changed. I was thrown into utter confusion.
hunks.sol: But the System’s voice in my ears hadn’t changed. Neither had the dozens of error messages floating in the air. Confusion seized me.

hunks.baseline: No—it had happened before, but only when I was in the middle of an important Quest, and even then it hadn’t happened like this.
hunks.sol: No—it had, but only when I was in the middle of an important Quest. Even then, it hadn’t happened like this.

hunks.baseline: *System error? Temporary maintenance?*
hunks.sol: *System error? Temporary Maintenance?*

hunks.baseline: An update, sure. But I’d never heard of anything like that.
hunks.sol: An update, sure. But I’d never heard of anything like this.

hunks.baseline: A groan slipped from my lips on instinct. I bit down hard and shouted over and over in my mind.
hunks.sol: A groan escaped me. I bit down hard and shouted over and over in my mind.

hunks.baseline: The holographic windows that poured out with every command showed only the words “System error.” Faced with this unbelievable reality, all I could do was stare blankly and take it in.
hunks.sol: Holographic windows spilled out with every command, each displaying the words “System error.” Faced with this unbelievable reality, all I could do was stare and try to take it in.

hunks.baseline: Actually, if I had to name one more thing I could do, it was let the person whose presence had drawn close to the door know that he was an unwelcome guest before he entered my room.
hunks.sol: Actually, there was one more thing I could do: let whoever had reached my door know they weren’t welcome before they came in.

hunks.baseline: Without even looking, I assumed it was Hyuk Mujin. If it wasn’t him, I figured it had to be one of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.
hunks.sol: I assumed it was Hyuk Mujin without even looking. If it wasn’t him, it had to be one of the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.

hunks.baseline: But my guess was just as spectacularly wrong as I’d been when I tried to Logout.
hunks.sol: But my guess was just as wrong as I’d been about Logging Out.
